full_text_en:
Hebei Shengda Yongqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. v. China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Tianjin Branch and Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Bank Acceptance Draft Agreement

【Ruling Summary】

Article 32 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where the parties enter into a contract in written form, the contract is formed when the parties sign or affix their seals thereto." Therefore, the effect of the parties' signatures or seals on the contract is to indicate that the content of the contract reflects the true intentions of the parties, and the parties shall enjoy the rights and perform the obligations under the contract accordingly. At the same time, the signatures or seals of the parties on the contract also serve to enable the counterparty to the contract to be assured of the identity of the other party to the transaction, thereby determining the parties to the contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 35

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Hebei Shengda Yongqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 19 Yunshan Road, High-tech Zone, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Sheng, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Kejian, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Weiqiang, employee of the company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Tianjin Branch, domiciled at No. 14 Nanjing Road, Hexi District, Tianjin.

Person in Charge: Guo Danghuai, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Feng Minshi, employee of the bank.

Agent ad litem: Shen Yongxi, lawyer of Tianjin Jiabang Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 175 Chaoyang North Road, National High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Baoding City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Administrator of Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Xie Yuanxun, lawyer of Beijing King & Wood Law Firm.

The appellant, Hebei Shengda Yongqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengda Yongqiang Company), having appealed against the civil judgment (2006) Jin Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 0035 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court in the case of dispute over bank acceptance draft agreement with the appellees, China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Tianjin Branch (hereinafter referred to as CITIC Bank) and Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baoshuo Company), appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Qian Xiaochen, and Acting Judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu to hear the case. Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The Tianjin High People's Court found the following facts upon trial: On October 27, 2005, CITIC Bank, Shengda Yongqiang Company, and Baoshuo Company signed a tripartite "Confirmed Warehouse Business Cooperation Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the Cooperation Agreement), stipulating: CITIC Bank and Shengda Yongqiang Company shall enter into a "Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the Acceptance Agreement) numbered (2005) Yin Cheng Zi No. HC0418. In accordance with the Acceptance Agreement, after receiving a deposit of 30%, amounting to RMB 9.144 million, paid by Baoshuo Company, CITIC Bank accepted bank acceptance drafts numbered 01053183-86 for a total amount of RMB 30.48 million. The draft period was from October 27, 2005 to April 27, 2006, with overdue interest calculated at 6.786%. Pursuant to Article 3 and Article 6(3) of the Cooperation Agreement, Baoshuo Company provided joint and several, irrevocable, and unconditional guarantee liability for the said Acceptance Agreement. Upon maturity of the drafts, Shengda Yongqiang Company failed to pay the remaining 70% of the draft amount, totaling RMB 21.336 million, to CITIC Bank in accordance with the Acceptance Agreement, and Baoshuo Company also failed to perform its joint and several guarantee payment obligations under the Cooperation Agreement, resulting in an overdue loan with a principal of RMB 21.336 million. After deducting the interest on the deposit, the remaining principal of the said overdue loan was RMB 21,252,199.69. On June 18, 2006, CITIC Bank filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin High People's Court, requesting an order that Shengda Yongqiang Company repay the principal of RMB 21,252,199.69 and the corresponding overdue interest accrued until the date of actual payment, and that Baoshuo Company bear joint and several guarantee liability, and that the litigation costs, preservation fees, attorney fees, and other expenses be borne by Shengda Yongqiang Company and Baoshuo Company.

The Tianjin High People's Court held that the Cooperation Agreement and Acceptance Agreement involved in the case were both genuine expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate relevant legal provisions, and should be deemed valid in accordance with law. CITIC Bank fulfilled its obligation to issue and disburse the drafts in accordance with the agreement. However, upon maturity of the drafts, Shengda Yongqiang Company failed to perform its repayment obligation, and Baoshuo Company also failed to perform its corresponding guarantee liability, which constituted a breach of contract and should bear liability for breach. Although the "Undertaking" and "Undertaking Regarding Financing in the Form of 'Confirmed Warehouse'" issued by Baoshuo Company to Shengda Yongqiang Company submitted by Shengda Yongqiang Company to the court stipulated that all legal liabilities arising from the financing should be borne by Baoshuo Company, such an agreement between Shengda Yongqiang Company and Baoshuo Company did not have external effect, and Shengda Yongqiang Company could not rely on it to claim exemption from its repayment liability to CITIC Bank. In summary, in accordance with Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 108 and 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered a default judgment: 1. Shengda Yongqiang Company shall, within 10 days of the judgment taking effect, repay the overdue loan principal of RMB 21,252,199.69 under the bank acceptance drafts numbered 01053183-86 owed to CITIC Bank and the overdue interest on such amount from the draft maturity date to the date of payment under the judgment (to be executed in accordance with the contract terms). In case of delay, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. 2. Baoshuo Company shall bear joint and several guarantee liability for the above payment items. The case acceptance fee of RMB 116,271 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 106,781 shall be borne by Shengda Yongqiang Company. Since these two fees were prepaid by CITIC Bank, the court will not refund them; they shall be paid by Shengda Yongqiang Company to CITIC Bank during execution, with Baoshuo Company bearing joint and several payment liability.

The appellant, Shengda Yongqiang Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Tianjin High People's Court, appealed to this Court, contending: 1. The Cooperation Agreement did not reflect the appellant's true intention, lacked the essential elements for validity, and had no legal effect. First, the Cooperation Agreement stipulated that the board resolution of Party B was an integral part of the agreement, but no board resolution of the appellant was submitted, thus the Cooperation Agreement did not have the effect of a tripartite confirmed warehouse cooperation. Second, the delivery notice from CITIC Bank was not delivered to the appellant for acknowledgment in accordance with the Cooperation Agreement. Third, the deposit for the acceptance draft was paid by Baoshuo Company, and CITIC Bank did not accept the appellant's deposit as stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement. Fourth, the appellant had no interest under the Cooperation Agreement, contrary to the purpose of business operations. 2. The Cooperation Agreement lacked genuine meaning; in essence, it was a coordinated action between CITIC Bank and Baoshuo Company to circumvent financial regulations by varying the form of a loan. The so-called Cooperation Agreement was merely a fictitious form used by CITIC Bank and Baoshuo Company to achieve the purpose of borrowing and lending, circumventing financial regulations through a lawful form. Its essence was to indirectly grant a loan, using a lawful form to evade financial regulations, resulting in harm to the interests of the state and third parties. According to Chinese law, such a legal act should be deemed invalid. 3. The appellant was a victim in this case and should not bear civil liability. The Cooperation Agreement, the "Application for Issuance of Bank Acceptance Draft," and the Acceptance Agreement were executed by Baoshuo Company privately without the appellant's knowledge, after the appellant was deceived by Baoshuo Company into lending out its official seal, financial seal, and the seal of its legal representative. Pursuant to Article 58(3) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, such civil acts should be void. The appellant requested the court of second instance: 1. To set aside the civil judgment (2006) Jin Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 0035 of the Tianjin High People's Court in accordance with law; 2. To dismiss CITIC Bank's claims; 3. To order the appellees to bear all litigation costs in this case.

CITIC Bank did not submit a written defense but stated during the second instance of this Court: First, the civil judgment (2006) Jin Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 0035 of the Tianjin High People's Court found facts clearly and applied the law correctly; it was a fair judgment rendered in accordance with law. The appellant's entire appeal request should be dismissed. The specific reasons are as follows: 1. In the confirmed warehouse business involved in this case, there were primarily three types of legal relationships: (a) the sale and purchase relationship between the manufacturer and the distributor; (b) the bill financing relationship formed between the distributor and the creditor bank due to the application for issuance of a bank acceptance draft; and (c) the guarantee relationship between the manufacturer and the creditor bank. These three legal relationships have a certain connection but are essentially independent. Their connection lies only in that the bill financing relationship between the distributor and the bank provides a financial payment instrument for the distributor to fulfill its payment obligation under the sale and purchase contract. Additionally, the creditor bank can reduce the bill financing risk to the distributor by establishing a guarantee relationship with the manufacturer. Shengda Yongqiang Company did not deposit sufficient margin upon maturity of the bank acceptance draft, resulting in a advance payment by CITIC Bank. All of CITIC Bank's claims against Shengda Yongqiang Company have full legal and factual basis. 2. The Cooperation Agreement and Acceptance Agreement involved in this case all reflected the genuine intent of the parties, did not violate relevant provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and each agreement was actually performed; they are legally valid contracts. The appellee has performed its obligations of acceptance and payment in accordance with the relevant agreements. However, upon maturity of the drafts, the appellant failed to perform its obligation to deposit sufficient margin or repay the advance payment made by the appellee under the bank acceptance drafts, and Baoshuo Company also failed to perform its corresponding joint and several guarantee liability. These constitute serious breaches of contract, and liability for breach should be borne in accordance with law. The "Undertaking" and "Undertaking Regarding Financing in the Form of 'Confirmed Warehouse'" issued by Baoshuo Company to the appellant and submitted by the appellant to the court are not genuine, have no external effect, and are irrelevant to this case; they cannot be used as evidence. The appellee requests the second instance court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The findings of fact by the court of first instance are basically correct, except for the determination of the payer of the deposit, and this Court affirms them. Additionally, this Court finds: On October 27, 2005, Baoshuo Company (Party A), Shengda Yongqiang Company (Party B), and CITIC Bank (Party C) entered into a Cooperation Agreement, Article 3 of which stipulates: "The 'tripartite cooperation' referred to in this Agreement means: Party B, based on the 'Purchase and Sale Contract' signed with Party A, deposits a certain percentage of margin with Party C and applies for issuance of a bank acceptance draft, which is used exclusively to pay the purchase price to Party A. Party A shall deliver goods to Party B based on Party C's formal notice, with the first delivery not exceeding the amount of margin deposited by Party B with Party C. Party B shall promptly supplement the margin with sales funds, and the cumulative notice of delivery by Party C to Party A shall not exceed the balance of the margin account. This process is repeated until the margin account balance reaches or exceeds the amount of the bank acceptance draft. If Party B fails to make full payment upon the maturity of the acceptance draft, Party A shall bear joint and several guarantee liability for the difference between the face amount of the acceptance draft due by Party B and the total amount of the delivery notices issued by Party C, as well as for overdue interest and penalty interests arising from overdue acceptance." The parties also made provisions regarding terms used in the contract, delivery handling procedures, payment and overdue handling upon maturity of the bank acceptance draft, liability for breach of contract, etc. Shengda Yongqiang Company affixed its official seal and the personal seal of its legal representative Zhou Sheng to the agreement. On the same day, Shengda Yongqiang Company submitted to CITIC Bank the "Application for Issuance of Bank Acceptance Draft" and simultaneously paid a deposit of RMB 9.144 million. CITIC Bank then accepted the bank acceptance drafts numbered 01053183-86 for a total amount of RMB 30.48 million, which were signed and received by Baoshuo Company. On the same day, CITIC Bank issued a delivery notice numbered sdbs051101, which was signed and sealed by Shengda Yongqiang Company to confirm receipt. On the same day, Baoshuo Company made an undertaking to Shengda Yongqiang Company: "Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd. urgently needs to handle a certain accounting transaction, and therefore borrows the official seal, financial seal, and the personal seal of the legal representative of Baoding Shengda Plastic Products Co., Ltd. (the original name of Shengda Yongqiang Company). We hereby undertake as follows: 1. For accounting purposes only. 2. To ensure that no interests of Baoding Shengda Plastic Products Co., Ltd. will be harmed. 3. To independently assume all liabilities. 4. To compensate for all losses if this undertaking is breached." On October 30, 2005, Baoshuo Company issued another "Undertaking Regarding Financing in the Form of 'Confirmed Warehouse'" to Shengda Yongqiang Company, stating: "Hebei Baoshuo Co., Ltd. is in need of a loan of RMB 34 million due to a shortage of funds for production and operation. However, given the current economic condition of Baoshuo Co., Ltd., it is difficult to obtain a bank loan. Therefore, after consultation with CITIC Industrial Bank Tianjin Branch, it was decided to change the loan method and adopt the form of 'confirmed warehouse' financing with Baoding Shengda Plastic Products Co., Ltd. as the drawer. We therefore undertake to Baoding Shengda Plastic Products Co., Ltd. as follows: 1. The entire sum shall be used and benefited by Baoshuo Co., Ltd. 2. Upon maturity of the drafts, the payee, Baoshuo Co., Ltd., shall repay. 3. All expenses incurred shall be borne by Baoshuo Co., Ltd. 4. If the drawer defaults upon maturity, Baoshuo Co., Ltd. shall independently bear the corresponding consequences and shall be liable for clearing the relevant debts with all its assets. It is guaranteed that Baoding Shengda Plastic Products Co., Ltd. shall not bear joint liability. 5. If this undertaking is breached, compensation shall be twice the losses."

During the second instance of this case, Baoshuo Company entered into bankruptcy proceedings.

This Court holds: The issue in dispute in the second instance of this case is whether Shengda Yongqiang Company should bear liability to CITIC Bank for repayment of the debt under the Cooperation Agreement, which bears its official seal and the personal seal of its legal representative, and the bank acceptance drafts numbered 01053183-86 issued in its name. Synthesizing the grounds of appeal of Shengda Yongqiang Company, it contends that it should not bear liability for two reasons: First, the Cooperation Agreement did not represent its true intention; Second, Baoshuo Company and CITIC Bank acted in malicious collusion, harming its interests, and the Cooperation Agreement should be declared invalid.

Regarding whether the Cooperation Agreement represented the true intention of Shengda Yongqiang Company. According to Article 32 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China: "Where the parties enter into a contract in written form, the contract is formed when the parties sign or affix their seals thereto." The effect of signing and sealing here is to indicate that the content of the contract represents the intention of the party that signed or affixed its seal, and that the party enjoys the contractual rights and performs the contractual obligations accordingly. In particular, it serves to assure the counterparty to the contract of the identity of the other party to the transaction, thereby determining the parties to the contract. In this case, the Cooperation Agreement and the documents related to the bank acceptance drafts all bear the official seal or the personal seal of the legal representative of Shengda Yongqiang Company, which should be deemed to represent the true intention of Shengda Yongqiang Company. Shengda Yongqiang Company appealed, arguing that its official seal, financial seal, and the personal seal of the legal representative were borrowed under deception by Baoshuo Company, and thus the related civil acts should be void. In this regard, this Court holds that Shengda Yongqiang Company lent out the relevant seals based on Baoshuo Company's undertaking. Regardless of whether Baoshuo Company's conduct amounted to deception, the relationship of lending the seals existed between Shengda Yongqiang Company and Baoshuo Company, and Baoshuo Company's undertaking only had effect between those two companies. For the protection of transactional security, unless it is proved that the counterparty, CITIC Bank, acted in bad faith, Shengda Yongqiang Company's argument that the seals were borrowed under deception cannot be used to oppose CITIC Bank's claim for rights under the contract. Regarding the issue of the board resolution of Party B, which is stipulated in Article 11 of the Cooperation Agreement as an inseparable part of the agreement, this Court holds: Based on the textual interpretation of this clause, if a board resolution of Party B existed, it would serve as a component of the Cooperation Agreement and provide certain corroborative evidence. However, the failure to submit a board resolution merely constitutes the omission of an attachment to the contract and does not affect the formation or validity of the contract. Regarding the issue of the receipt of the delivery notice under the Cooperation Agreement, Shengda Yongqiang Company's claim that the delivery notice was not delivered to it for acknowledgment is inconsistent with the facts. In the receipt column of the delivery notice numbered sdbs051101, the seal of Shengda Yongqiang Company was affixed, which is deemed to indicate that the company had received the delivery notice. Regarding the issue of who paid the deposit of RMB 9.144 million, representing 30% of the bank acceptance drafts, this is a matter of contract performance. The check used to pay the deposit bore the financial seal and the personal seal of the legal representative of Shengda Yongqiang Company, which should be considered as payment made by Shengda Yongqiang Company. Moreover, the law never prohibits a third party from performing contractual obligations on behalf of another. Even if the deposit was paid by Baoshuo Company, it does not affect the validity or continued performance of the contract. As for whether Shengda Yongqiang Company benefited from the Cooperation Agreement, the agreement shows that the company could secure a certain period's supply of goods from Baoshuo Company through the confirmed warehouse business, which itself constituted consideration. The fact that it ultimately suffered severe losses is attributable first to its act of lending out its seals, and second to the risk brought about by Baoshuo Company's business failure and entry into bankruptcy proceedings. None of the grounds of appeal of the appellant, Shengda Yongqiang Company, are sufficient to negate the validity of the Cooperation Agreement.

Regarding the issue of whether there was malicious collusion between CITIC Bank and Baoshuo Company. First, Baoshuo Company's undertaking to Shengda Yongqiang Company was that the lending of the seals would not cause losses to Shengda Yongqiang Company. If Baoshuo Company had not failed in its business operations, it should have repaid the corresponding debt to Shengda Yongqiang Company in accordance with its undertaking. Moreover, three days after signing the Cooperation Agreement, on October 30, 2005, Baoshuo Company issued another "Undertaking Regarding Financing in the Form of 'Confirmed Warehouse'" to Shengda Yongqiang Company. Even if the fact of lending the seals was established and the company was unaware of the purpose of using the seals, by that time the company had become aware and did not raise any objection, which should be deemed as acceptance of the arrangement. Second, even if it is determined that Baoshuo Company committed fraud, there is no evidence to prove that CITIC Bank knew or should have known that Baoshuo Company borrowed Shengda Yongqiang Company's seals to enter into the contract, nor is there any evidence showing that CITIC Bank and Baoshuo Company had any contact of intent regarding the borrowing of the seals. Third, regarding the issue of whether financial regulations were violated, loans serve a financing function, and bank acceptance drafts also have a financing effect. The mere commonality between the two in this respect cannot be used to determine an intention to circumvent financial regulations. Therefore, Shengda Yongqiang Company's claim that CITIC Bank and Baoshuo Company acted in malicious collusion to circumvent financial regulations, harming the interests of the state and third parties, and that the Cooperation Agreement should be deemed an invalid civil act, is also untenable.

In summary, the grounds of appeal of the appellant, Shengda Yongqiang Company, are not sustainable. The facts found in the original judgment are basically clear, and the application of the law is basically correct. Pursuant to Article 153(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court orders as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 116,271 shall be borne by the appellant, Hebei Shengda Yongqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Qian Xiaochen

Acting Judge: Liu Min

Acting Judge Yang Zhengyu

July 24, 2007

Clerk Yuan Hongxia
